title: Average Orders Divisor Sums and Representation Counts

items.title: The harmonic sum is log x plus gamma plus O(1/x)
items.strategy: Compare each unit interval with the integral of 1/t, identify the monotone remainder defining gamma, and bound the tail by an integral of x^{-2}.

items.title: Dirichlet's hyperbola method for summatory convolutions
items.strategy: Expand the summatory convolution as the finite lattice sum over ab <= x, split the lattice points into the arms a <= U and b <= V, and subtract the overlap rectangle counted twice.

items.title: The summatory divisor-counting function is x log x plus (2 gamma - 1)x plus O(sqrt x)
items.strategy: Use tau = 1 * 1, apply the hyperbola identity with U = V = sqrt x, and keep the floor and overlap terms until the final O(sqrt x) estimate is collected.

items.title: The summatory logarithm is x log x minus x plus O(log x)
items.strategy: Write the sum as log(floor x !), compare it with the integral of log t on [1,N] and [1,N+1], and evaluate the antiderivative t log t - t by the product rule and the FTC.

items.title: The average order of tau is log n
items.strategy: Compare the summatory tau estimate with the summatory logarithm asymptotic and match the common x log x main term.

items.title: The summatory divisor-sum function is pi squared over 12 times x squared plus O(x log x)
items.strategy: Rewrite sum_{n <= x} sigma(n) by exchanging divisor and quotient roles, replace the inner consecutive sum by y^2/2 + O(y) with y = floor(x/d), and split the result into Basel and harmonic pieces.

items.title: The average order of sigma is (pi squared over 6)n
items.strategy: Sum the linear comparison function exactly and compare its leading term with the summatory sigma estimate.

items.title: The summatory totient function is 3 over pi squared times x squared plus O(x log x)
items.strategy: Recover phi(n) = sum_{d|n} mu(d)(n/d) from the published divisor-sum theorem and Mobius inversion, reverse the finite order of summation, and use the same consecutive-sum expansion together with Basel and harmonic estimates.

items.title: The average order of Euler's totient is 6n over pi squared
items.strategy: Sum the linear comparison function and compare its leading term with the totient summatory estimate.

items.title: Ordered coprime pairs in a box have asymptotic density 6 over pi squared
items.strategy: Partition the coprime pairs by their maximum coordinate: m = 1 contributes one pair, and each m > 1 contributes 2 phi(m); then apply the summatory totient estimate.

items.title: The proportion of pairs in {1,...,n}^2 that are coprime tends to 6 over pi squared
items.strategy: Divide the preceding asymptotic by n^2 and let n tend to infinity.

items.title: The normalized two-square count is multiplicative with the expected prime-power values
items.strategy: Use the odd-to-even doubling bijection for powers of 2, the prime-power representation facts and prime uniqueness for odd primes, and the primitive product/factorization bijection to make r_2/4 multiplicative and compute its prime-power cases.

items.title: The divisor formula for the two-square representation count
items.strategy: Let g(n) = sum_{d|n} chi_4(d), prove directly that g is multiplicative by splitting divisors of coprime products, compute its three prime-power cases, and compare with the normalized r_2 lemma.

items.title: The average order of the two-square representation count is pi
items.strategy: Apply the hyperbola method to the divisor formula for r_2, use the periodic bounded partial sums of chi_4, and identify the odd harmonic difference with the Gregory-Leibniz series for pi/4.

title: Average Orders Divisor Sums and Representation Counts — Examples

items.title: A small lattice decomposition for Dirichlet's hyperbola method
items.strategy: Choose a small x, list the lattice points ab <= x, split them into the two hyperbola arms and their overlap, and verify the exact counting identity.

items.title: The divisor summatory estimate through several small values
items.strategy: Compute sum_{n <= x} tau(n), compare it with x log x + (2 gamma - 1)x, and tabulate the residual at the sqrt x scale.
